analysis.title: October ECB cheat sheet: French malaise shouldn't prompt a dovish turn
key_insights: ING expects the ECB to hold rates at 2.5% at the 29 October meeting. A hike is close to zero chance priced in.
The key question is whether French and other European bond turmoil triggers a dovish shift in ECB messaging. ING does not think it has.
ING expects the ECB to leave the door open for a December hike with a broadly neutral and balanced message. This should shield rates and the euro from a major adjustment.
Signalling that a December hike is 'likely' would be a slightly hawkish surprise in ING's view, even though markets price in 20bp.
A more dovish tone on further tightening would probably be the first line of defence against more bond volatility, before any bond-buying measure.

An unexpected 25bp hike would be a bigger surprise. Without clear second-round inflation risks, it could trigger a broader risk-off move, wider French spreads and lower equities. 10yr Bund yields could fall on growth concerns.
Rates have started to deviate from their tight correlation with oil, but global factors remain an important driver. Risk sentiment is fragile because of the French turmoil and renewed AI jitters.

The euro is 1-1.5% undervalued to short-term fair value and has become less sensitive to French spread moves. ING sees the balance of risks on the downside for EUR, but its baseline is a broadly stable euro after Thursday.
ING prefers EUR/USD to return to the 1.120-1.130 area over the coming weeks.

tension_points.bull_case: A firmer commitment to a December hike would nudge a hawkish repricing and support the euro, with more than 20bp already priced in so the reaction is contained.
tension_points.bear_case: French bond turmoil and fragile sentiment could force a dovish rethink, with a softer tone on tightening the first defence against bond volatility.
tension_points.what_invalidates: A more dovish tone on further tightening at the press conference, or an unexpected 25bp hike that triggers risk-off.
